summary: Tested the 'Fila de envio' send queue end to end without sending anything. Backend: 13/13 pytest pass. New API tests: 5 against the live API using fake TESTQ_ rows, all removed afterwards. New temp-DB tests: 4. The 4 iteration-2 delivery-claim regression tests still pass. Verified: GET /api/queue structure, stats math and the rendered reminder body. Cancelling selected items touches only the chosen delivery and reminder; an already-sent row is untouched and a second cancel does nothing. {all:true} cancels every pending delivery and reminder (guarded to run only because no real pending items existed). Both endpoints return 401 without a token, and a bad payload returns 422. A delivery cancelled during the pace wait is never sent. The failure path does not overwrite 'cancelled'. In the scheduler, with fake painel users expiring in 3 days and 2s pacing, cancelling the 2nd run item skips only that client, and its daily key is set to 'cancelled'. Cancel-all interrupts the pacing wait at once (only the first client was sent). Frontend at 1920x1080, all checks pass: sidebar nav to /fila, all 4 stat cards correct (5/0/3/2), 5 rows, expand shows the WhatsApp bubble plus last error and id. The open row stays open after the 3s auto-refresh. All 4 filters show the right counts, and select-all/unselect-all update the 'Cancelar selecionados (N)' count. The dialog's 'Voltar' keeps the selection; 'Sim, cancelar' removes 2 rows, shows a toast, updates stats and adds a 'CANCELADA' history row. 'Cancelar tudo' leaves the empty state and disables the button. No JS page errors.

minor.issue: History reads only notification_deliveries, so cancelled reminders (sent=3) and cancelled run items disappear with no trace. The 24h counts also leave them out. A cancelled delivery shows created_at as its time because there is no cancelled_at column.

Cancelling a run item only changes memory. The daily key is set to 'cancelled' only when the loop reaches that item. If the backend restarts mid-run, cancelled clients that were not reached yet are planned again and sent on the next hourly run. Persist the key at cancel time, e.g. have cancel_run_items return the keys and have the router call set_setting.

When send_notification returns False (template disabled, deduped, etc.), the item is labelled 'queued', which misleads the admin. The first item of a run is sent with no wait, so it can never be cancelled.

issues: The 12-column row grid is cramped. The status pill overlaps 'Tentativa 1/5', the 'STATUS' header is clipped, and names and titles are truncated to 3-5 chars. Use a stacked card layout below md.

action_items: Optional: show cancelled reminders and run items in the 'Últimos envios' history, and add a cancelled_at timestamp
Optional: persist the run-item cancellation (daily notified key = 'cancelled') immediately in /api/queue/cancel so it survives a restart
Optional: responsive mobile layout for queue rows
critical_code_review_comments: queue.py imports DB_PATH by value (from database import DB_PATH). That works in production, but patching database.DB_PATH will not reach the router.
Selection is computed from the filtered items only. Items selected under another filter are silently dropped from 'Cancelar selecionados'. That is acceptable, but the count can surprise users.
The _attempt success path writes 'sent' with no status guard. That is correct, because the message actually went out even if it was cancelled mid-send.
seed_data_creation: TESTQ_ rows (3 deliveries, 2 reminders, 1 sent delivery) were inserted into the real whatsflow.db only during tests. All have been DELETED (verified 0 remaining). The scheduler tests used a temp DB copy.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=<url> pytest tests/test_send_queue_api.py tests/test_send_queue_cancel_tempdb.py tests/test_delivery_queue_claim_tempdb.py. To seed or clean the UI: python3 tests/testq_seed.py seed|cleanup|none. The cancel-all API test skips itself if real pending items exist. Never trigger notify endpoints, because these are production customers.
